attacks.claim: S7's 'hoist ONE ModifierContext per frame and mutate ctx.timeMs per voice' changes aliasing semantics: today chain.ts:44 allocates a FRESH ctx per applyModifierChain call (per range), so a modifier whose apply() retains the ctx reference (e.g. into its createState slot) sees a stable snapshot; after the hoist every retained reference aliases one mutated object whose timeMs is whatever the LAST voice wrote. No test or the heap-delta harness can catch a capturing modifier — the harness measures allocation, not aliasing.
attacks.evidence: packages/core/src/modifiers/chain.ts:44 `const ctx: ModifierContext = { model, timeMs, dt };` is per-call today; compositor.ts:244 calls applyModifierChain per range inside the voice loop with per-voice `timeMs - v.bornAtMs`. The plan's S7 verification lists typecheck, suites, and a heap-delta harness — none of which fail for a modifier that stores ctx.
attacks.repair: Add to S7's verification: grep every modifier definition for any assignment of the ctx parameter into state or module scope (`ctx` escaping apply), and document that ModifierContext is a borrowed, per-call-invalidated view; if any modifier retains it, keep a per-voice (not per-frame) construction for that path.

attacks.claim: S6's parity spec is internally inconsistent: it says 'the eight `() => base` entries must be exactly the kinds S1's switch reached via default' and then lists TEN kinds (trigger, all, random, sequence, chance, toggle, delay, scope, output, envelope). An implementer cannot execute 'eight entries' against a ten-kind list without guessing which statement wins.
attacks.evidence: Plan S6 verification text: 'the eight `() => base` entries must be exactly the kinds S1's switch reached via default (trigger, all, random, sequence, chance, toggle, delay, scope, output, envelope)' — that parenthetical is 10 items. Source confirms 10: trigger-flow-projection.ts:31-52 handles switch/play/modifier/mix/cc/note/osc/randomMod/lfo (9 arms), leaving 10 of the 19 canonical kinds to `default: return base`.
attacks.repair: Correct S6 to 'the ten () => base entries' and keep the enumerated list as authoritative; the golden table test already makes any miscount fail, so this is a text fix.

attacks.claim: S4's rule that each per-kind interface carries 'only its own kind's fields as required (not optional)' is both a runtime lie and a sequencing breaker: kind-specific fields that are OPTIONAL on the flat interface (ccController, ccChannel, oscAddress, noteNumber, modifierId, playType, canvasScene, lfo, …) exist on persisted shows only sometimes, and nothing in the plan adds normalize-time defaulting for them; and once they are required on the union arms, the flat GraphNode (which S13/S14 have not yet retired) stops being assignable to GraphNodeUnion, so S6's core-dispatch narrowing (wave 3) and S9's inspectors (wave 4) cannot typecheck while stores/tests still hand them flat nodes.
attacks.evidence: types.ts flat interface marks these fields optional (triggerNodeSignature reads `n.ccController ?? ''`, `n.modifierId ?? ''`, `n.playType ?? ''` at trigger-flow-projection.ts:36-49 — the ?? exists because the fields can be absent); modulation-graph's nodeModSource applies `??` defaults (finding repeated-switches-0002 / opus S12 enumerate ten of them as 'load-bearing back-compat for graphs authored before each field existed'). S4's own text: 'carrying only its own kind's fields as required (not optional)'. TS assignability of {kind:'cc', ccController?: number} to an arm requiring ccController fails.
attacks.repair: Preserve each kind-specific field's current optionality on its union arm (required-ness may only match the flat interface), or route every ingress through a narrowing normalizer that provably defaults each newly-required field — and state which, per field, in S4.

attacks.claim: S15 contradicts the rollback strategy: the step's intent says it 'changes the on-disk/clipboard string format', while rollback_strategy claims 'no step in this plan performs an irreversible data migration… no user data can be stranded'. A show saved by a post-S15 build in the new encodeScopeTarget format is unreadable by every pre-S15 build (and by a post-revert build), and the 'version-gated codec' that would prevent this is asserted in one clause but designed nowhere — no version field, no dual-write, no fixture proving old builds read new saves.
attacks.evidence: Plan S15 intent: 'it changes the on-disk/clipboard string format and touches the compositor's per-frame parseHoopTarget call'; rollback_strategy: 'S15's persisted-format change is additive (decode accepts both…)' — decode-both protects the NEW build reading OLD data, not old builds reading new saves, which is exactly the stranding case the strategy denies. Contrast fable-plan's S4, which commits a forward-compat fixture proving the pre-step sha loads post-step saves.
attacks.repair: Keep the persisted string format byte-identical: decode/encode ScopeTarget only at the persistence boundary while still writing the existing `drum#h,h` string (escaping added only behind an explicit version bump with a forward-compat fixture test at the pre-S15 sha), or drop the on-disk change from S15 entirely.
